query: Current status of U.S.-Argentina 123 civil nuclear cooperation agreement negotiations as of August 2026. Has a new Agreement for Cooperation been signed or is a signing ceremony scheduled?
answer:
## Summary

**Direct answer: No new Agreement for Cooperation has been signed, and no signing ceremony has been scheduled or dated publicly.**

The key finding is a **10 August 2026 TN report** (widely syndicated, but a single original anonymously-sourced story) that Casa Rosada considers the text "closed" at the technical level — reportedly finished at the February 2026 JSCNEC meeting — with Cancillería now coordinating signature logistics with Washington, targeting signature before end-2026.

Three things sharpen the picture:

1. **The official record is thinner than the press claim.** The 5/6 March joint statement commits only to "swiftly *complete* negotiations on the text" — not that the text is complete, initialed, or agreed *ad referendum*. The Argentine claim of a finished text is not corroborated by any U.S. source.

2. **Every U.S. channel is silent.** No State Dept item since 5 March; no 2026 Presidential Determination for Argentina (the only one is Saudi Arabia, 28 July); no Congressional transmittal; DOE/NNSA's 123 page still dated 11 July 2025. The Saudi case shows the contrast — signed 22–23 July, Federal Register determination within a week, immediate DOE/WSJ/ANS coverage.

3. **Timing has margin but not much.** Expiry is 16 October 2027 (423 days out), and entry into force needs 90 days of *continuous session* in Congress after signature — realistically 4–6 calendar months. Milei's remaining U.S. calendar: UNGA in September, **Washington on 14 October**, Miami G-20 on 14–15 December. No source connects any trip to a signing.

Two caveats worth flagging: whether the successor needs fresh Argentine congressional ratification (the 1997 one did, via Ley 24.862) is unaddressed anywhere I looked, and the 1992→1996→1997 precedent shows an agreed text can sit unsigned for years.

key_facts: NO new U.S.-Argentina 123 Agreement has been signed as of 19 August 2026, and no signing ceremony date, venue, or signatories have been publicly announced.

The most recent official bilateral statement remains the 19th JSCNEC joint statement, released by the U.S. State Department on 5 March 2026 and by Argentina's Cancilleria on 6 March 2026, committing only to 'swiftly complete negotiations on the text' of a new Agreement for Cooperation - not stating the text was complete or initialed.

On 10 August 2026, TN (Todo Noticias, journalist Ignacio Salerno) reported that Casa Rosada sources say the drafting was 'closed' between technical teams, that the new wording was actually finished at the 25-27 February 2026 JSCNEC meeting, and that the current phase is diplomatic coordination for signature with a goal of signing before the end of 2026.

The 10 August 2026 report was syndicated verbatim across at least nine Argentine outlets (El Litoral, Diario Panorama, NoticiasNet, ANRoca, Metadata, DiarioYA, Cholila Online, Piramide Informativa, Enterate Noticias) - it is ONE original anonymously-sourced report, not multiple independent confirmations.

No U.S.-side confirmation exists in any channel: no State Dept media note since 5 March 2026; no 2026 Presidential Determination for Argentina in the Federal Register; no Congressional transmittal document; DOE/NNSA 123 Agreements page last updated 11 July 2025.

The DOE/NNSA 123 Agreements page lists Argentina as 16 October 1997 / 16 October 2027 with NO rolling-extension clause, unlike Australia, Canada, Switzerland, Euratom, Morocco, Turkey and Vietnam - so the agreement lapses absolutely on expiry.

The comparison case shows what a signing looks like: the U.S.-Saudi Arabia 123 Agreement was signed 22-23 July 2026 by Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, with a Presidential Determination published in the Federal Register on 28 July 2026 and immediate DOE/WSJ/ANS coverage. Nothing comparable exists for Argentina.

Escalation of language across JSCNEC meetings: 18th meeting (30 Sep - 3 Oct 2024, Buenos Aires) delegations 'committed to COMMENCE negotiations'; 19th meeting (25-27 Feb 2026, Washington) delegations 'reaffirmed their commitment to SWIFTLY COMPLETE negotiations on the text'. No 20th JSCNEC meeting has been announced.

Delegation heads at the 19th JSCNEC: Gonzalo Suarez, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary for Nonproliferation Policy, Bureau of Arms Control and Nonproliferation, State Dept; and Dr. Federico Ramos Napoli, Argentina's Secretary of Nuclear Affairs, Ministry of Economy.

U.S. procedural path after signature: Presidential approval and determination under AEA sec.123 b., Nuclear Proliferation Assessment Statement, transmittal to Congress, then 30 days of continuous session for committee consultation (sec.123 b.) plus 60 days of continuous session for review (sec.123 d.) = 90 days total, entering into force absent a joint resolution of disapproval.

The 1997 agreement required Argentine Congressional approval via Ley 24.862 (August 1997). Whether the successor agreement requires fresh Argentine legislative ratification is NOT clarified in any public source found.

Milei's remaining 2026 U.S. calendar (confirmed by official sources, reported 9 Aug 2026): UN General Assembly in New York in September; Washington DC on 14 October for a Hispanic Heritage Month conference; Miami on 14-15 December for the G-20 leaders' summit. Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno accompanies both the October and December trips. No source links any trip to a nuclear signing.

The U.S.-Argentina Agreement on Reciprocal Trade and Investment (ARTI, February 2026) contains Article 4.3(3): 'Argentina shall not purchase any nuclear reactors, fuel rods, or enriched uranium from certain countries' - a binding nuclear-procurement constraint already in force in a separate signed instrument.

Regional contrast: Ecuador signed a Nuclear Cooperation MOU (NCMOU) with the U.S. on 1 April 2026; Paraguay signed an NCMOU on 4 August 2026. Both are MOUs that do not authorize nuclear exports, a rung below a 123 Agreement. Argentina already holds full 123 status.

Critical Argentine commentary (El Estrategico, 4 August 2026) argues Argentina enters the renegotiation without a documented sovereign position: CNEA budget cut ~40%, science and technology spending at 0.22% of GDP against a legal mandate of 0.45%, Pilcaniyeu enrichment reactivation unfunded, CAREM construction halted, and the Plan Nuclear Argentino containing no reference at all to the 123 Agreement renegotiation.

Argentina's bilateral nuclear momentum with the U.S. is otherwise strong: joined FIRST as a contributing partner in September 2025 (first Latin American country in that tier), hosted the FIRST LAC workshop 2-4 June 2026 in Buenos Aires, and CNEA co-hosted an NNSA Office of International Nuclear Security workshop in June 2026.

Related U.S. private investment in Argentina's nuclear sector in 2026: Meitner Energy's USD 1.2 billion, 300 MWe ACR-300 SMR at Atucha (announced July 2026, backed by the Ansari Group), and NANO Nuclear Energy's USD 230 million+ plan for the Dioxitek Formosa uranium plant (April 2026). TN explicitly notes the Meitner project is independent of the 123 Agreement.

One syndicated version of the 10 August report (ANRoca/NoticiasNet) erroneously renders the expiry as 'vence el proximo 16 de octubre' without the year; the correct date confirmed by TN, DOE/NNSA and Cancilleria is 16 October 2027.
No prediction markets exist on this question - searches of Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold returned no relevant markets.

Historical precedent for delay: the 1992 U.S.-Argentina text was reached ad referendum on 3 September 1992 but was not signed until 29 February 1996 and did not enter into force until 16 October 1997 - roughly five years from agreed text to entry into force.
